result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and sidewalks on all corners. However, the lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions results in a relatively wide crossing distance and potential sightline issues due to parked cars.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked near the intersection corners can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the curb line near the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Wide intersection geometry
hazards.description: The open nature of the intersection without curb extensions may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Installing bulb-outs would shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars before they enter the travel lane.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restricting parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection equipped with sidewalks, a marked crosswalk, and pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, safety is compromised by parked vehicles obstructing sightlines and visible pavement degradation in the foreground.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner block the sightlines between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection along the curb

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Pavement
hazards.description: The asphalt in the foreground and within the intersection shows significant cracking and wear, which can create uneven surfaces for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the intersection

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel line markings to continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to approaching drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with multi-story brick buildings and sidewalks on both sides. While the environment appears to be a low-speed residential area, it lacks marked pedestrian crossings and features significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles along the curbs.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along both sides of the street block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might attempt to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely within the visible area.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate pedestrian right-of-way and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near intersections or mid-block crossing points to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly constrained by a large tree and utility pole that obstruct the sidewalk, forcing a narrow passage. While a pedestrian signal and traffic light are present, the sidewalk pavement is in poor condition with visible cracks and debris.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree and a utility pole occupy most of the sidewalk width, forcing pedestrians into a very narrow path.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is cracked, uneven, and covered in debris, creating trip hazards.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to provide a clear, accessible path around the tree and utility pole.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Resurface the sidewalk to provide a smooth, level walking surface free of trip hazards.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way at the intersection.
